answer.says: Shri Hegde, I must confess the confusion of the allotment. I am the philosopher, not the Joint Secretary, though the clerk has made us of one name. Ramesh, I am aware the wage is due. I have only ninety-six rupees in my pocket tonight, but the state's money in the imprest is not yet released. I will settle your account from the vouchers as soon as the Directorate clears them. For now, I am hungry. If you have any cold food or bread, I will pay you from my remaining cash, but I cannot ask you to cook what I cannot immediately settle.
answer.thought: The presence of Hegde and Ramesh compresses the two major contradictions of my stay: the bureaucratic error that places me here, and the economic dependency that binds me to the caretaker. I have no food because I have no money, and I have no money because the state is slow. It is a dialectic of hunger and bureaucracy.
